outcomes.measure_name: Median initial direction error of pointing responses (angular error)
outcomes.higher_is_better_evidence: Their errors increased abruptly at the onset of the adaptation phase, and then gradually dropped again. Most importantly, adaptive improvement was more pronounced for young than for old subjects.
outcomes.operationalization: Angular error (median initial direction of each response per episode, i.e. between movement onset and peak velocity) during the last of the 15 pointing episodes with +60° rotated visual feedback (adaptation phase, episodes 6–20 in Fig. 1); the paper reports no block average, only the per-episode group means plotted in Fig. 1 plus exponential fits of the adaptation time course.

outcomes.measure_name: Root mean square error between target and cursor during tracking (RMSE)
outcomes.higher_is_better_evidence: Clearly, tracking errors were higher during visual rotation; this increase was substantial in control subjects, and was followed by a gradual improvement, particularly for young participants.
outcomes.operationalization: Tracking RMSE per 50-s episode (excluding the initial 0.5 s of each episode) during the rotated-feedback tracking episodes of the control subjects, who received no prior pointing adaptation; late adaptation = the final rotated tracking episode of the control series in Fig. 2 (thin lines, episodes from 11 onward). Methods state control subjects performed "five tracking episodes with +60° rotated feedback on the second day".

sources.locator: Fig. 2, rotated-feedback portion (episodes 11 onward), thin lines: thin triangles = young control, thin squares = old control; last plotted rotated episode
sources.quote: Fig. 2 Mean tracking errors of young (triangles) and old (squares) subjects before and during exposure to rotated visual feedback. Bold lines represent experimental subjects which adapted to the rotation in a pointing task before being transferred to tracking; thin lines represent control subjects not pre-adapted with pointing
sources.notes: Control-group RMSE values exist only in this figure; the caption does not state what the plotted error bars represent. Note the possible mismatch between Methods ("five tracking episodes with +60° rotated feedback") and the x axis of Fig. 2, which extends to episode 20.

sources.locator: Fig. 2, first rotated-feedback tracking episode (episode 11), thin lines (young and old control subjects)
sources.quote: we were interested in the transfer of adaptation from pointing to tracking, as revealed by the first tracking episode under rotated feedback
sources.notes: Initial exposure point of the control series; relevant if the review uses the first rotated episode rather than the last.

sources.locator: Fig. 2, baseline veridical-feedback tracking episodes 1–10, thin lines (young and old control subjects)
sources.quote: Those subjects only executed ten tracking episodes with veridical feedback on the first day and five tracking episodes with +60° rotated feedback on the second day.
sources.notes: Pre-rotation tracking baseline (mean RMSE of episodes 6–10 is the baseline used by the authors for the above-baseline error).

sources.locator: Results, ANOVA on above-baseline tracking error (factors Age and Procedure)
sources.quote: submitted the outcome to an ANOVA with the between-factors Age (young, old) and Procedure (experimental, control). Only the effect of Procedure was significant (F(1,43)=144,09, P<0.001).
sources.notes: Above-baseline error defined as RMSE in episode 11 minus mean RMSE in episodes 6–10; no group means printed, and no Age effect statistic is reported numerically.

parsed.notes: Page numbers are PDF sheet positions (article printed pages 259–263 correspond to sheets 1–5). The paper prints almost no numeric values for the two outcomes: all pointing-error and tracking-RMSE group means live only in Fig. 1 (sheet 3) and Fig. 2 (sheet 4). Fig. 1 error bars are explicitly standard deviations (caption); Fig. 2's caption says nothing about its error bars, so their type is UNKNOWN. The only text numbers bearing on adaptation magnitude are the exponential-fit parameters (sheet 3) and the pooled 54-senior adaptation magnitude 0.49±0.21 (sheet 4), the latter from a supplemented sample with no matching young value. No aftereffect phase exists for the control tracking sample (dataset 2), so no aftereffect outcome is listed there. Trail-making, reaction-time and questionnaire results are not protocol outcomes and were not mapped.
